MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM  -3-  NC: 2025:KHC-K:7365
CRL.P No. 201585 of 2025 HC-KAR  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)

The present petition is filed by the in-laws of the second respondent/complainant under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, seeking quashing of the proceedings pending in C.C.No.278/2025 (arising out of Crime No.96/2023 registered by Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, Kalaburagi District)
on the file of I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Kalaburagi, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 and 109 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.

sentences.text: 2. Petitioners, who are the in-laws, siblings-in-law and the husbands of the siblings of accused No.8--the husband of the complainant have approached this Court seeking quashing of the criminal proceedings.

Their principal contention is that in the written complaint dated 22.07.2023, the second respondent herself has categorically acknowledged that she had been residing NC:
2025:KHC-K:7365 HC-KAR separately with her husband/accused No.8.
All allegations pertaining to neglect, marital discord and harassment are specifically directed only against accused No.8.
There are absolutely no individual or specific allegations against any of the present petitioners.

Despite this, they are arrayed as accused for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 and 109 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3.
The petitioners further point out that, even in an earlier complaint lodged by the second respondent, serious allegations were attributed only against her husband/accused No.8.

Notwithstanding this consistent narrative, the present petitioners who do not share the common roof with the complainant and against whom no overt acts are alleged are now compelled to face a criminal trial.
It is in this background that the petitioners seek quashing of the proceedings.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7365 HC-KAR 4.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State.
Perused the material on record.

5. On meticulous examination of the written complaint dated 22.07.2023, two significant features emerge:
Firstly, the complainant admits that accused No.8/husband had left for abroad Abeda vs The State Of Karnataka on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147589735/
3 without informing her in 2012, returned in 2014, and thereafter lived with the complainant till 2015.

entities.text: Abeda vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Again in 2015, he left for abroad and came back only in 2017.

Upon his return in 2017, due to differences between accused No.8 and his father, the family effected a partition of residence, whereunder three separate rooms were allotted exclusively for the use of accused No.8 and the complainant.
The written complaint further reveals that they continued to live together in the allotted portion for some time.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7365 HC-KAR

The complaint next states that in November 2021,
after accused No.8 returned from his subsequent stay in the Gulf region, he allegedly quarreled with the complainant, leading to frequent marital discord.

The complainant thereafter attributes that at the instance of accused No.8, the petitioners more particularly the father- in-law and mother-in-law used abusive language and allegedly threw her out of the shared household.

6. A careful reading of the complaint in its entirety, however, reveals that the complainant explicitly acknowledges that there had been a family partition, pursuant to which a separate and exclusive residential portion comprising three rooms had been allotted in the share of accused No.8.
This itself indicates that the petitioners were living separately and did not share the common household with the complainant.

7. The complaint also repeatedly refers to the prolonged stays of accused No.8 in the Gulf region,
which NC: 2025:KHC-K:7365 HC-KAR appears to be the primary reason for the marital discord between the spouses.
The allegations against the petitioners are, therefore, bald, omnibus, and unsubstantiated, lacking any particulars of date, time, place or specific acts.

The mere assertion that the petitioners "instigated" accused No.8 or used abusive language without any specific instances cannot form the foundation for criminal prosecution under Section 498A IPC and other allied offences.

8. If this Court declines to exercise its inherent jurisdiction, the petitioners who include aged parents-in- law of 66 and 69 years and married sisters-in-law residing in their respective matrimonial homes would be unnecessarily subjected to the rigmarole of criminal prosecution.
Accused Nos.5 and 6, who are the husbands of accused Nos.3 and 4 and who do not even reside under the same roof, are also implicated without any specific accusation.
Even accused No.7, who is a distant relative, is arrayed as an accused without any foundational material.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7365 HC-KAR 9.

In the circumstances, continuation of proceedings against the petitioners would amount to abuse of the process of law, particularly when the complainant has a clear and effective remedy to proceed legally against her husband/accused No.8, against whom the entire allegations of cruelty and neglect are consistently directed.

sentences.text: In view of the foregoing discussion and the settled principles governing the exercise of inherent powers, this Court is satisfied that the case on hand warrants interference under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

Permitting the prosecution to continue against these petitioners, in the absence of any cognizable material or specific allegations, would result in grave injustice and would be contrary to the very object for which the inherent power is vested in this Court, namely, to prevent abuse of process and to secure the ends of justice.
Accordingly, the proceedings NC: 2025:KHC-K:7365 HC-KAR deserve to be quashed insofar as the petitioners are concerned.

11. Accordingly, this Court passes the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is allowed.

ii. The proceedings in C.C. No. 278/2025, arising out of Crime No.96/2023 of Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, Kalaburagi District, pending before the I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Kalaburagi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 and 109 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, are hereby quashed insofar as the present petitioners are concerned.
